why: p07's filtered intro opens into a tight, moody breakbeat groove at 0:21, while p17 is a pretty music-box lullaby rocking between two chords with nothing arriving.
p10 is a dark late-night trip-hop groove with a bar-29 breakdown that rebuilds to a snare roll, while p17 is a sweet bell-toned lullaby sketch whose only event is a chord left ringing at 0:36.
p07's cool, hypnotic groove lands hard when the drums come in at 0:21, while p20 mostly sways through a pastel game-music loop and only darkens for its Fm9 stretch at 0:56.

p07 gives a real arrival when the filter opens and the drums hit at 0:21, while p19 is hypnotic and bittersweet and lifts a tone at 0:54, but it is a short, slightly tense cue that never lands with much weight.

Both are gentle and pretty, but p09 at least pulls you in when the deep bass enters at 0:24 and the Lydian guitar arrives at 0:41, while p17 just repeats its music-box phrase apart from the ringing pause at 0:36.
p18's dark pads swell into a hard beat drop at 0:20 and later fall away into drumless breakdowns, while p09 is sunny focus-music arpeggios that barely change and fade out at 2:03.

p06 is melancholy and rainy-window, with a full-level arrival at 0:10 and drumless floating interludes at 1:46, while p16 is cheerful, bouncy game music at one level whose wistful turn at bar 23 is brief.
p18 is dark and immersive, with its beat dropping in after the pad riser at 0:20 and a drumless breakdown at 2:54, while p08 is an upbeat game-action rush that stays at one level from 0:26 on.
p10 is a moody late-night head-nod that breaks down and rebuilds to a snare roll at 1:40, while p20 starts as a pastel, swaying game loop and only turns darker at 0:56.
p06 is sad and immersive, with a beat that lands at 0:10 and drops out to breathe at 0:58, while p17 is a pretty lullaby-like sketch that repeats one phrase for a minute.

Both are dark and hypnotic, but p18's full beat drops in hard after the pad swell at 0:20 and it has more drumless breaths later, while p10's beat enters only 3 dB up at 0:11 and the track is over in two minutes.

p06 stays melancholy throughout, with a real arrival at 0:10 and floating drumless interludes, while p20 sways through a pretty pastel loop and only reaches its darker peak at 0:56 before a quick fade.

Both open muffled and then drop into a groove, but p18 also breathes with its stop bar at 1:06 and its drumless colour change at 1:38, while p07 repeats its first groove section after 1:28 once the hook has gone.
p08 builds from quiet piano to the full band crashing in at 0:26 and has a stop-time section at 1:06, while p16 is cheerful and bouncy at one flat level with only a one-bar break at 0:58.
p07 is cool and moody, with a filter-sweep intro that lands in a tight groove at 0:21, while p16 is a cheerful, relentless game cue whose wistful chromatic turn at bar 23 is its only shadow.
p08 at least delivers an energetic full-band arrival at 0:26, while p17 is a sweet music-box lullaby that only pauses on a ringing chord at 0:36.
p20 has a beat and a darker Fm9 climax at 0:56, while p09 stays sunny, calm focus music whose bass entry at 0:24 is only a few dB lift.

Both are melancholy grooves with drumless breaths, but p18's riser dropping into a dark beat at 0:20 and its colour switch at 1:38 pull you in a little further than p06's wistful guitar loop, even with p06's arrival at 0:10.

p19's one-note ostinato is hypnotic and bittersweet, with a lift at 0:54, but it is short and a bit tense, while p06 sinks deeper into sadness with a full arrival at 0:10 and a slowing, unresolved ending at 2:43.
p19 is wistful and hypnotic, with drums dropping in and out and a whole-step lift at 0:54, while p09 is bright, sunny new-age looping that fades at 2:03 without going anywhere.

p08's full band crashing in at 0:26 is a real arrival, but it then runs as an upbeat game rush at one level, while p19's bittersweet ostinato breathes with drumless stretches at 0:45 before the lift at 0:54.
p10 is dark and late-night, with a breakdown at bar 29 that rebuilds to a snare roll, while p16 is a bright, bouncy game cue at one level apart from a one-bar break at 0:58.
p10's dark trip-hop groove pulls you in more, with its brightening at 0:54 and its breakdown and rebuild at 1:11, than p19's slightly tense, one-note ostinato, despite p19's nice lift at 0:54.
p08 is flat but driving after the band hits at 0:26, while p20 spends most of its time in a pastel, swaying loop before a darker peak at 0:56 that comes too late.
p16 is cheerful but energetic, with a wistful chromatic turn at bar 23, while p09 is gentle, sunny focus music that repeats its first half almost verbatim from 1:05.
